subject: Physics
title: Electric Potential and Capacitor
learningOutcomes: Define and calculate electric potential (work done per unit positive charge in bringing a small test charge from infinity to the point) and use V = Q/(4πε₀r) for the potential due to a point charge.
Use the fact that the electric field at a point is equal to the negative of the potential gradient at that point.
State how the concept of electric potential leads to the electric potential energy of two point charges and use U = Qq/(4πε₀r).
Define and calculate capacitance as applied to parallel plate capacitors, including the effect of a dielectric (relative permittivity).
Derive and apply the formulae for the combined capacitance of capacitors in series and in parallel.
Determine the energy stored in a capacitor from the area under the potential–charge graph and use E = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C to solve problems.
Analyse charging and discharging of a capacitor through a resistor; use τ = RC and Q = Q₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)) or Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC).
List the uses of capacitors in household appliances (flash guns, refrigerators, electric fans, rectification circuits, radio and TV sets).
Illustrate how bioelectricity is generated in animals (cell membrane, ion channels, resting and action potentials).
State that aquatic species such as Electrophorus electricus can naturally generate external electric shocks (electrogenic animals).
Explain, with examples of animals, that electroreception is the ability to detect weak naturally occurring electrostatic fields.

sections.heading: Electric Potential Energy and Electric Potential
sections.body: The energy needed to move a charge against an electric field is called electric potential energy. For a test charge q₀ between oppositely charged plates the force is F = q₀E, and the change in potential energy equals the work done: U_A − U_B = W_BA. Electric potential is the potential energy per unit charge, V = U/q, so it is a property of the location in the field and does not depend on the size of the test charge. The potential difference ΔV = ΔU/q₀ is the work done per unit positive charge, and ΔU = q₀ΔV. Its unit is the volt: 1 V = 1 J/C.

sections.heading: Potential Due to a Point Charge
sections.body: In a constant field the potential difference is ΔV = −EΔr, so the electric field equals the negative of the potential gradient: E = −ΔV/Δr. For a point charge Q the field is not constant, so the path is divided into tiny steps and the work of every step is added; the middle terms cancel. Bringing a charge q from infinity to distance r gives the potential energy U = Qq/(4πε₀r), and the potential at distance r is V = Q/(4πε₀r). The potential falls as 1/r, and every point at the same distance from an isolated charge has the same potential.

sections.heading: Capacitors and Capacitance
sections.body: A capacitor stores electric energy. A parallel plate capacitor has two identical parallel plates a distance d apart with a dielectric between them. A battery places +Q and −Q on the plates, and the charge stays bound by mutual attraction. The charge is directly proportional to the voltage, Q = CV, so the capacitance is C = Q/V. The unit is the farad: 1 F = 1 C/V. Using σ = Q/A, E = σ/ε₀ and E = V/d, the capacitance in vacuum is C_vac = Aε₀/d. A dielectric multiplies this by the relative permittivity, C_med = Aε₀ε_r/d, where ε_r = C_med/C_vac.

sections.heading: Combinations of Capacitors
sections.body: In series, every capacitor carries the same charge and the voltages add, so 1/Cₑ = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + 1/C₃; for two capacitors Cₑ = C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂), and N identical capacitors give C/N. The equivalent capacitance is smaller than the smallest one. In parallel, every capacitor has the same voltage and the charges add, so Cₑ = C₁ + C₂ + C₃, and N identical capacitors give NC. The equivalent capacitance is larger than the largest one, which is why capacitors are joined in parallel to store a large amount of energy.

sections.heading: Energy Stored and Uses of Capacitors
sections.body: The potential–charge graph of a capacitor is a straight line through the origin, and the energy stored is the area of the triangle under it: E = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C. A capacitor can release all its energy very quickly, unlike a battery, which releases energy slowly through chemical reactions. Capacitors filter unwanted frequencies in radio and TV sets, reduce the ripple voltage in rectification circuits, store and release energy in camera flashes, keep the compressor of a refrigerator running and increase the speed of an electric fan.

sections.heading: Charging and Discharging an RC Circuit
sections.body: In an RC circuit a capacitor charges or discharges through a resistor. While charging, the current is highest at the start and falls to zero when the capacitor voltage equals the e.m.f.; the charge grows as Q = Q₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)) with Q₀ = Cε. While discharging, the charge falls as Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC). The time constant τ = RC is the time for the charge to reach 63.2 % of its maximum while charging, or to fall to 36.7 % of its initial value while discharging. A smaller time constant means faster charging and discharging.

sections.heading: Bioelectricity
sections.body: Bioelectricity is the generation or action of electric currents or voltages in biological processes. The cell membrane is semipermeable and acts like a capacitor, with charged ions on opposite sides. When K⁺ ions diffuse out of a nerve or muscle cell through ion channels, a net negative charge is left inside, giving a resting potential of about 50 mV. When a cell is stimulated, ion channels open, positive charges enter and action potentials are produced. Electrogenic animals such as the electric eel (Electrophorus electricus, up to 860 V) generate shocks, while electroreceptive animals such as sharks, rays, echidnas, platypuses, bees, spiders and dolphins detect weak electrostatic fields.

definitions.definition: The energy needed to move a charge against an electric field.
The potential energy per unit charge at a point in an electric field, V = U/q.
The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another, keeping the charge in electrostatic equilibrium.
The potential difference between two points when one joule of work is done in moving one coulomb of charge between them.
The rate of change of potential with displacement; the electric field is the negative of the potential gradient.
An electronic device used to store electric energy (charge).
The ratio of the charge on a plate to the potential difference across the capacitor, C = Q/V.
The capacitance of a capacitor that stores 1 coulomb of charge with a potential difference of 1 volt between its plates.
The insulating medium (air or a sheet of some insulator) between the plates of a capacitor.
The ratio of the capacitance with a dielectric between the plates to the capacitance of the same capacitor in vacuum.
The product RC of an RC circuit; the time in which a charging capacitor reaches 63.2 % of its maximum charge.
An electrical pulse produced when the inside of a stimulated cell becomes more positively charged and triggers further electrical currents.

examTips: Series: the same charge, voltages add, 1/Cₑ = Σ1/C and Cₑ is smaller than the smallest capacitor. Parallel: the same voltage, charges add, Cₑ = ΣC. Mixing these up is the most common FBISE mistake.
Always convert μF, nF, pF and mm or cm into SI units (F and m) before using Q = CV, E = V/d or C = Aε₀/d — most lost marks in numericals are unit slips.
Remember the two RC values: 63.2 % of the maximum charge after one time constant while charging, and 36.7 % of the initial charge left while discharging.
Know the three forms of stored energy, E = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C, and choose the one that uses the quantities you are given.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What is the SI unit of capacitance?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Capacitance is charge per unit voltage, so 1 farad = 1 coulomb per volt.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Electric potential at a point is defined as the:
practiceQuestions.explanation: V = U/q: potential energy divided by the charge.

practiceQuestions.prompt: How does the electric potential due to a positive point charge change as the distance from the charge increases?
A 4 μF capacitor is charged to 12 V. How much charge does it store?
Which quantity is the same for every capacitor in a series combination?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In series the same charge Q is on each capacitor and the voltages add.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Two capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. What is the equivalent capacitance?
Capacitors of 2 μF, 3 μF and 5 μF are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent capacitance?
How much energy is stored in a 10 μF capacitor charged to 20 V?
After one time constant, what fraction of its maximum charge does a charging capacitor hold?
Filling the space between the plates of a capacitor with a dielectric of relative permittivity εr changes the capacitance by a factor of:
The electric potential at a point depends on the size of the test charge placed there.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — a test charge of any size has the same electric potential at a given location; only its potential energy changes.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a parallel combination of capacitors, every capacitor has the same potential difference across it.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — the battery supplies the same voltage to each branch, and the charges add.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The ratio of the charge on a plate of a capacitor to the potential difference across it is called ______.
The time constant of an RC circuit is τ = ______ (type the two letters).
Electric eels can deliver shocks of up to ______ volts.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The textbook states up to 860 V.

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange the events in the correct order as a capacitor charges through a resistor.

items: The current falls gradually towards zero
Charging stops with the maximum charge Q₀ = Cε
The current is at its highest value and the capacitor voltage is zero
The potential difference across the capacitor reaches the e.m.f.
The switch is set at point 1 and the battery starts charging the capacitor
Charge builds up on the plates and repels the arriving charge
correctOrder: The switch is set at point 1 and the battery starts charging the capacitor
The current is at its highest value and the capacitor voltage is zero
Charge builds up on the plates and repels the arriving charge
The current falls gradually towards zero
The potential difference across the capacitor reaches the e.m.f.
Charging stops with the maximum charge Q₀ = Cε

sequencingActivity.explanation: Charging starts fast and slows down until V equals the e.m.f. and the current becomes zero.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance of 5 μF. Its plate area is doubled and the plate separation is halved. What is the new capacitance?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: C = Aε₀/d, so doubling A and halving d multiplies C by 2 × 2 = 4: 4 × 5 = 20 μF.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A 6 μF and a 3 μF capacitor are connected in series across an 18 V battery. What is the potential difference across the 3 μF capacitor?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Cₑ = 2 μF, Q = CₑV = 36 μC on each. V = Q/C = 36/3 = 12 V across the 3 μF capacitor (and 6 V across the 6 μF).

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A capacitor stores energy E at a voltage V. If the voltage is tripled with the same capacitance, the energy stored becomes:
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: E = ½CV² ∝ V², so tripling V multiplies E by 9.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Which change makes a capacitor charge more slowly through a resistor?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: τ = RC; a larger R gives a larger time constant, so the capacitor charges and discharges more slowly.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Why does the cell membrane of a nerve cell behave like a capacitor?

options: K⁺ ions diffuse out through ion channels, leaving a net negative charge inside, so opposite charges sit on the two sides of the membrane
It stores energy chemically like a battery
It allows all ions to pass freely

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Opposite charges separated by the semipermeable membrane store energy as a resting potential of about 50 mV — like the plates of a capacitor.
